texts.at-0001: Round money only with round_money Always round monetary Decimal results with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent); never use Python's round() or a bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.
texts.at-0002: Use to_money and ZERO for money math In ledgerly/invoice.py, coerce unit prices with ledgerly.money.to_money and seed sums with ledgerly.money.ZERO rather than plain Decimal literals, matching line_total and invoice_total.
texts.at-0003: Raise BillingError with stable snake_case codes Validation failures in `ledgerly/invoice.py` raise `BillingError(code, detail)` from `ledgerly.errors` with codes like `invalid_state`, `invalid_quantity` and `negative_amount`; reuse these codes instead of inventing new exception types.
texts.at-0004: Exclude bool when validating integer inputs When validating integer parameters, reject `bool` explicitly (`isinstance(quantity, bool)`) before the `isinstance(quantity, int)` check, since `True`/`False` are ints in Python and would otherwise pass.
texts.at-0005: Normalize datetimes with ensure_utc before arithmetic In ledgerly, always pass incoming datetimes through `ledgerly.clock.ensure_utc` before comparing or doing arithmetic (see `current_period` in `ledgerly/subscriptions.py`); apply it to both the argument and `sub.started_at`.

item.title: Use money helpers for all amounts
item.content: Convert every monetary input with `ledgerly.money.to_money` and round results with `ledgerly.money.round_money`; never do raw float arithmetic on prices. `to_money` rejects floats with `BillingError("float_amount")`, so callers must pass Decimal or str.
